newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brasilia says it won't buckle to states over debt.
newsitem.headline: Brasilia says it won't buckle to states over debt.

text.p: The Brazilian government will negotiate on a case-by-case basis with states seeking to restructure their debts with Brasilia, but it will not be pushed into a collective deal, a Finance Ministry official said.
"The government's view is that the negotiation of (medium and short-term debts) should be done on a case by case basis," Pedro Parente, the ministry's executive secretary, said.

Earlier on Tuesday, governors from two states and the Federal District handed in to Congress a draft copy of a bill that would give the states better conditions for the repayment of a reported 46 billion reais of debt.

The bill was said to include the lengthening of payment terms for the debt to 30 from 20 years and a cut in the maximum amount states may spend on debt servicing and retirement to six percent of receipts from an existing 11 percent. Parente said the government would demand that states take measures to improve their respective fiscal situations before being offered improved debt terms.
But the government was sympathetic to other proposals included in the bill, like new rules to speed up recovery of funds through the justice system, he said.
